script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Sci-Fi
Theme: identity

Begin screenplay.

Title: "Neuronauts"

FADE IN:

EXT. CITYSCAPE - NIGHT

The city is alive with neon lights and holographic advertisements. We see PEOPLE in futuristic clothing walking on FLYING CARPETS.

NARRATOR (V.O.)
In a world where consciousness can be transferred from one body to another, identity becomes a matter of perception.

INT. LAB - DAY

DR. LENA SPARKS (mid 30s, intelligent and passionate) and her team are working on a neural interface.

DR. SPARKS
Gentlemen, today we're going to test the Neuronaut program for the first time. It's a risky procedure, but the potential rewards are immense.

TECHNICIAN 1
Are you sure, Dr. Sparks? The ethical implications...

DR. SPARKS
(smiling)
We've discussed this. We're all volunteers. Trust me, this will be a historic moment in human history.

INT. TEST SUBJECT ROOM - DAY

JASON (late 20s, eager and curious) lies down on a bed, wearing the neural interface.

DR. SPARKS
Jason, you're about to become the first Neuronaut. You'll experience a sensation similar to sleep, and when you wake up, you'll be in a new body.

JASON
I'm ready. Let's do this.

INT. NEURAL INTERFACE ROOM - DAY

Dr. Sparks activates the interface.

INT. NEW BODY - INNER WORKINGS - DAY

Jason's consciousness leaves his original body and enters a new one. He experiences disorientation and confusion.

INT. NEW BODY - LIVING ROOM - DAY

Jason wakes up in a strange living room, disoriented but eventually realizes he's in a new body. He explores the house, discovering he's now in the body of an elderly man.

INT. DR. SPARKS' OFFICE - DAY

Dr. Sparks and her team are ecstatic about the successful transfer. They discuss the implications and potential applications of the Neuronaut program.

INT. JASON'S FAMILY HOME - NIGHT

Jason, now in the elderly body, returns to his family home. He's greeted warmly by his wife and children, who are initially shocked but eventually accept him.

INT. DR. SPARKS' LAB - DAY

Dr. Sparks and her team plan the next Neuronaut transfer. They decide to transfer the consciousness of a terminally ill patient into a healthy body.

INT. HOSPITAL ROOM - DAY

The patient, MIKE (early 30s, dying of a rare disease), is connected to the neural interface. Dr. Sparks initiates the transfer.

INT. MIKE'S NEW BODY - INNER WORKINGS - DAY

Mike's consciousness leaves his dying body and enters a new one. He experiences a moment of euphoria, finally free from his suffering.

INT. MIKE'S NEW BODY - DAY

Mike wakes up, confused and disoriented, but eventually realizes he's in a new body, healthy and free from his disease.

INT. DR. SPARKS' LAB - DAY

Dr. Sparks and her team are elated by the success of the transfer. They discuss the potential implications of saving lives and extending them.

INT. JASON'S NEW BODY - NIGHT

Jason, now in a younger, healthier body, struggles with his new identity. He experiences a crisis of self and wonders if he's truly the same person.

INT. MIKE'S OLD BODY - DAY

Mike's old body lies in the hospital bed, empty and lifeless. Dr. Sparks and her team discuss the ethical implications of the Neuronaut program and the potential consequences of identity transfer.

FADE OUT.

The end.
